lens: Senior reviewer for IEEE T-ASE / T-RO / RA-L. Focus: are the competitors real published algorithms (coverage planners, uncertainty-aware or chance-constrained planners, tracking controllers, conformal-prediction planners), or only margin rules on one planner? Also: system-level evaluation, planning-control coupling, and whether the method beats state of the art. I checked this against the code (exp_lib.py, exp_main.py, exp_real.py, calibrate_conformal), the CSVs in results/, and every PNG in figures/.
verdict: REJECT in its current form (resubmission encouraged) at T-RO or RA-L; MAJOR REVISION at best at T-ASE or Computers and Electronics in Agriculture. The user's critique is correct, and the problem goes deeper than presentation. All 14 'baselines' in exp_lib.py are functions that map one shared vector of run-level scores to one scalar lambda. They feed one greedy boustrophedon planner, one LQR-I controller and one simulator. For each field, every method therefore sits on the same curve P(no-miss | lambda), and the methods differ only in where they land on it. I checked the numbers: with n=100, CE-U uses the 91st order statistic of the scores, while the scenario approach (beta=0.01) uses the 96th, which is also what PAC/training-conditional conformal uses at delta=0.05. So the headline 'CE-U beats scenario/CVaR/DRO' compares a marginal guarantee with a PAC guarantee on the same score. It is not a better algorithm. This is also why the figures collapse: invalid rules sit at P=0, valid ones cluster at 0.9-1.0, and CE-U, CE-A and CE-pair coincide because none of them moves the cost-reliability frontier. The practical gain is small: CE-U plans 32.8 passes per field against 33.4 for scenario (paddy v3), about 1.8 percentage points of overlap. A Q1 reviewer will also make these points. (i) Validity in simulation is guaranteed by construction, because calibration and test runs come from the same simulator. (ii) The real-robot replay is invalid as implemented: time-consecutive passes are treated as adjacent rows when the row indices show they are not. The reference is a lattice fitted to the same passes. The 30-40% overlap operating point is not credible. (iii) The zero-miss target is agronomically questionable: fixed 10 cm overlap already misses only 1.33 per ten thousand (0.013%) of the area, and CE-U nearly doubles overlap (3.7% to 6.6%) to remove slivers. (iv) CE-A, the tube-MPC coupling and the fixed-point theorem have no empirical case where they matter. To reach Q1, the paper should present conformal erosion as a planner-agnostic certification layer and benchmark it against published planners (Fields2Cover, Hameed 2016 3D side-to-side, Jin and Tang 2011, Bretl and Hutchinson 2013), controllers (Lenain slip-adaptive, tube MPC, cautious GP-MPC) and conformal-planning methods (Lindemann 2023, Cleaveland 2024, PAC-CP, risk allocation). It also needs an algorithmic contribution that actually moves the frontier, such as certified driving-angle optimisation or controller co-design. It should be evaluated at equal reliability with system-level metrics, on an independent higher-fidelity plant plus corrected or new real data. Short answer in Chinese for the user: 你说得对——目前只是在同一规划器上比较不同的λ选取规则（本质上是同一组分数的不同分位数），这只是比较了种类，没有比较算法，图重合到一个点也是这个结构造成的。不补齐已发表的规划、控制和共形规划算法，并且不做出能推动前沿的算法贡献，很难中一区。

major_issues.issue: The competitors are not algorithms. All 14 baselines (fixed overlap, slope rule, Gaussian/empirical/conformal pointwise, Gaussian chance constraint, Cantelli, scenario, CVaR, Wasserstein DRO-CVaR, worst-case, CE-pair, GBM-QR, CQR) are scalar lambda-selection rules applied to the same score vector (scoresU in exp_main.py), the same greedy planner core.plan, the same LQR-I controller and the same simulator. They all lie on one per-field curve P(lambda). The claimed win over scenario is a marginal-versus-PAC choice: order statistic 91 versus 96 of the same 100 scores, and PAC-CP at delta=0.05 also picks order statistic 96. The measured effect is 0.6 passes per field (CE-U 32.8 vs scenario 33.4 on paddy v3).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A T-ASE/T-RO reviewer will say the paper compares estimators of one quantile, not planning algorithms. No published coverage planner, uncertainty-aware planner or tracking controller is compared, so state of the art is never tested. Comparing a marginal guarantee with a PAC guarantee and reporting lower overlap is an apples-to-oranges comparison.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Rebuild the benchmark in three layers and treat CE as a plug-in on each. (A) Planners: Fields2Cover (pip install fields2cover; v2.1.0 confirmed on PyPI) with brute-force angle search, boustrophedon/snake routes and Dubins/continuous-curvature turns; a re-implementation of Hameed et al. 2016 3D side-to-side spacing; Jin and Tang 2011 3D-terrain effective width; Choset BCD or the Bahnemann GTSP boustrophedon for non-convex fields; Bretl and Hutchinson 2013 robust erosion. Run each with its native overlap rule and with CE. (B) Controllers: pure pursuit, Stanley, LQR-I, the Lenain 2006 slip-observer adaptive controller, and tube MPC with deterministic tube erosion; each with its native margin and with CE. (C) UQ/planning: PAC-CP (the fair counterpart of scenario), SAA (Luedtke and Ahmed), Gaussian risk allocation (Ono and Williams 2008 / Blackmore 2011), Lindemann 2023 union-bound CP (CE-pair is this; credit it), Cleaveland 2024 optimised-weight max score, cautious GP margins, and CQR. The main metric should be cost at equal reliability: sweep each method's own knob, interpolate the overlap (and path length/time) at realised P=0.90, and report the regret against a per-field oracle lambda* computed from the test runs. State the guarantee type explicitly (marginal, PAC, or none) in a table column.
major_issues.effort: About 2-3 weeks in total, all feasible here: F2C integration 1 day (PyPI wheel); Hameed and Jin-Tang re-implementation 2-3 days on the existing DEM and shapely; Lenain controller 1 day; tube MPC 2-3 days (cvxpy, pytope, casadi on PyPI); PAC-CP, SAA, risk allocation, GP and Cleaveland 2 days; reruns 2-3 days of CPU.

major_issues.issue: The real-robot replay (CitrusFarm) is invalid as implemented. exp_real.windows() takes K time-consecutive passes and places them at lateral positions yk = h + k*2h, i.e. treats them as adjacent rows. The stored row indices contradict this: seq 02 drives rows 0,-5,-10,...; seq 03 steps by 2; seq 04 drives 0,6,1,5,2,4,3; seq 06 drives 0,2,4,6. Only seqs 01, 05 and 07 are at least 92% adjacent, and repeated rows (6,6 / -6,-6) also appear. The reference y_ref is a lattice least-squares fitted to the same passes. The Jackal was most likely teleoperated (verify in Teng et al. 2023), so this is not tracking error of a planned line. Errors are large: sd 0.365 m, p95 |e| 0.73 m, max 1.73 m. The result is lambda of about 0.8 m on a fictitious 6 m implement and 30-40% overlap for every valid method. CE-U also fails 3 of 10 out-of-distribution splits (minimum 0.833) where scenario and PAC hold.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: The only real-data evidence does not measure autonomous execution error. The pass-to-pass pairs are not physical neighbours, and the operating point (36% overlap) is agronomically meaningless. A reviewer who checks the data will discount the whole real-world claim, and RA-L/T-RO require real autonomous execution.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Build windows only from runs of physically adjacent rows using p['row'] (|row diff| = 1, no repeats). Drop seqs 02, 03, 04 and 06, or use only their adjacent sub-runs, and report the reduced n honestly. (2) Relabel the experiment 'manual/teleoperated driving regime, reference = fitted row lattice' and move it to a robustness section, not the headline. (3) Look for real autosteer logs on GitHub or S3: ISO 11783-10 TaskData/ISOXML sample logs, AgGateway ADAPT sample data, AgOpenGPS field logs, PX4 ulog swath flights; all of these are unverified leads. (4) The most decisive Q1 addition is a small hardware experiment by the authors: any RTK-equipped mobile robot or mower executing at least 30 boustrophedon runs on flat and sloped turf with a real implement-width proxy, plus a calibrate-on-day-1 / test-on-day-2 split.
major_issues.effort: Fixing adjacency and rerunning: half a day. Searching for alternative logs: 1-2 days, outcome uncertain. A hardware experiment cannot be done in this environment; it takes the authors 2-4 weeks with a robot.

major_issues.issue: Validity results in simulation are tautological. Calibration and test runs are i.i.d. draws from the same authors' kinematic simulator (slip gain, roll compensation and OU roughness are set from orders of magnitude in the literature, not identified from data). Exchangeability therefore holds by construction, and 0.917 >= 0.90 only confirms that split conformal is implemented correctly. The in-field setting assumes n=100 past operations on the same field, which no farm has.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers will say the experiments prove a textbook property of split CP. The real questions are efficiency against competing algorithms, robustness when the deployed plant differs from the calibration source, and realistic sample sizes, and these are under-tested.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Add an independent higher-fidelity plant: either MuJoCo (PyPI 3.15.0) or PyBullet with a 4-wheel tractor on a DEM heightfield, or at minimum a dynamic bicycle model with Pacejka lateral tyre forces and gravity on side slope, written in numpy. (2) Run a model-mismatch test: calibrate on the kinematic sim and test on the dynamic plant, as a sim-to-real proxy, and report which methods break. (3) Make cross-field calibration with n in {5,10,20,50} the main setting and move in-field n=100 to the appendix. (4) Put the existing ablation, where the absolute-error score over-covers and the pointwise score fails, next to the shift results so validity claims rest on non-trivial cases.
major_issues.effort: Dynamic bicycle plant: 1-2 days. MuJoCo tractor: 4-6 days. Cross-field n-sweep reruns: 1-2 days of CPU. All feasible offline.

major_issues.issue: The target P(missed area = 0) is agronomically and economically questionable. A sub-millimetre gap at any 1 m cross-section counts as a failure. From the v3 tables: fixed 10 cm overlap has E[miss] = 1.33 per ten thousand (0.013% of area) at 3.7% overlap; CE-U has 0.45 per ten thousand at 6.6% overlap. CE-R, the risk certificate that would be the practical one, is 4.5x conservative (realised 6.1-6.7 per ten thousand against alpha = 30) because the loss bound B = 1.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Agricultural-engineering reviewers (CEA, Biosystems Engineering, T-ASE practitioners) will say the method nearly doubles input overlap to remove slivers worth 0.01% of the field, which is economically irrational. The certificate then looks like a solution to an artificial problem.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Generalise Lemma 1 to a gap tolerance: a gap counts only if its width exceeds delta and it persists for at least l metres along track. Use delta = 2-5 cm and l = 1-3 m, justified by spray-pattern overlap or seed-row spacing. The score becomes sup (e_{k+1} - e_k - delta)/(sigma_k + sigma_{k+1}), a one-line change in pair_scores and evaluate. (2) Add an economic objective: CNY/ha of overlap cost (seed, fertiliser, pesticide, time) against miss cost (yield loss per m2). Choose alpha for CE-R economically and make CE-R a main result. (3) Tighten B with a bounded-error controller, which also delivers the promised coupling (see the tube MPC issue), or use a data-driven bound via Learn-then-Test with Hoeffding-Bentkus instead of B = 1.
major_issues.effort: Tolerance version plus reruns: 1-2 days. Economic model from published input prices: 1 day.

major_issues.issue: The figures collapse into a single point for structural reasons, not cosmetic ones. P(no-miss) is bimodal (invalid rules at 0, valid ones at 0.9-1.0) on a linear [0,1] axis. CE-U and CE-A coincide because sigma is nearly uniform within fields at 30 m DEM resolution. CE-U and CE-pair are identical in the real-robot tables (both 0.916 / 36.3%). Every method shares the same P(lambda) curve. Fig. 3 titles are also stale: they say 19/10 fields, while the tables say 27/16, the v3 CSVs hold 60/37 fields, and the report says 40/40.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Main figures that show no separation between the proposed method and the strong baselines, and that collapse the proposed variants into each other, signal no contribution. Inconsistent field counts signal unfinished, cherry-pickable experiments.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use three new main figures. (1) An oracle-regret plane: x = coverage shortfall (target minus realised P, per field), y = overlap regret versus the per-field oracle lambda*. CE should sit near the origin, PAC/scenario at (0, +), and fixed rules at (-, -). (2) Frontier plots: overlap (or total path length or time) against realised miss probability on a log axis from 1e-3 to 1. Each method traces a curve as its knob is swept; mark the target. Show that algorithmic competitors (F2C, Hameed, controllers) move the frontier while CE lands on it with a guarantee. (3) A paired-difference plot of CE-A minus CE-U overlap against within-field slope heterogeneity (CV of side slope), which shows when adaptivity helps. Put the trivially failing rules in a compact table or inset, not the main axis. Regenerate everything from one frozen run with one field count.
major_issues.effort: 1-2 days of plotting after the reruns; the oracle lambda* needs one extra lambda sweep per field (about 1 day of CPU).

major_issues.issue: The terrain-adaptive variant (CE-A) is a headline contribution with a null result. Wilcoxon p = 0.41 (paddy) and 0.90 (wheat); per-field overlap differs by only 0.6-1.2 percentage points (v3). The cause is the 30 m DEM on fields with a median of about 0.6 ha, so slope is nearly uniform within each field. A4 (stationarity across passes) also implicitly assumes homogeneity.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A contribution whose benefit cannot be shown on the paper's own data will be judged unsupported. The only positive evidence is a synthetic toy field.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Choose one or more. (a) Get real within-field heterogeneity: the USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM is on public AWS (s3://prd-tnm/StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/; I confirmed WA projects are listed), and US field boundaries are on source.coop S3 (fiboa/us-usda-cropland, confirmed listed). Use hilly Palouse wheat fields in WA/ID, where slopes reach 15-30%. (b) Make adaptivity act through the decision: side slope = slope * |sin(theta - aspect)|, so sigma depends on driving direction even at 30 m resolution. Add certified angle optimisation inside the F2C brute-force angle search, minimising certified passes or path length; this is a genuine new algorithm that moves the frontier. (c) Replace the heuristic sigma fit with a principled one: Cleaveland et al. 2024-style optimisation of normalisation weights on a held-out split, or Gibbs-Cherian-Candes conditional CP over a terrain function class. (d) If none of these works, demote CE-A to a remark.
major_issues.effort: (a) 2-3 days for the data pipeline. (b) 2 days with fields2cover. (c) 1-2 days with scipy linprog/milp. All feasible with the reachable networks.

major_issues.issue: Planning-control coupling is claimed but not delivered. The proposal's Theorem 4 corollary (tube MPC bounds B, robust invariant set) and innovation point 4 have no implementation. The controller study (fig8) only reports CE's own overlap per controller, with no baseline per controller and no co-design.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: For T-RO/T-ASE, coupling planning and control is the natural differentiator, and an unimplemented claim will be flagged as overclaiming. Reviewers will also ask whether a better controller (slip compensation) makes the certificate unnecessary.
major_issues.concrete_fix: (1) Implement linear tube MPC on the lateral error dynamics (d, psi, integral), with a disturbance set identified from calibration residuals; use cvxpy/OSQP and pytope for the RPI set. Compare deterministic tube erosion (lambda = tube radius) with CE plus tube MPC, and show the tightened B in CE-R. (2) Run a controller co-design: choose LQR weights or the lookahead to minimise CE-certified overlap rather than RMS error, and show that the best-RMS controller is not the best-certified-coverage controller. (3) Add the Lenain 2006 slip-compensated controller with fixed overlap as the strongest control-side competitor, to show whether CE is complementary or substitutable.
major_issues.effort: 4-6 days in total, feasible: cvxpy, osqp, casadi and pytope are all on PyPI.

major_issues.issue: Novelty is positioned against the wrong literature. The normalised max-over-time score is the score of Cleaveland, Lee, Pappas and Lindemann (AAAI 2024). Union-bound per-step CP (CE-pair) is Lindemann et al. (RA-L 2023). Erosion of the footprint for robust coverage is Bretl and Hutchinson (ICRA 2013). Skip/overlap-aware 3D swath placement is Hameed et al. (RAS 2016). CP for chance-constrained programs is Zhao et al. (CPP, 2024). Online adaptation in planning is Dixit et al. (L4DC 2023).
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: A conformal-prediction-for-robotics reviewer will see 'split CP on a max-normalised score, then erode by q' as incremental unless the paper names what is genuinely new.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Add a positioning table (problem, score, guarantee type, decision dependence, planner coupling). Claim novelty precisely on three things: Lemma 1 (gap if and only if relative pass-to-pass error, so common-mode error is harmless); plan-family dominance (Theorem 2), which covers the change in pass count N(lambda); and the monotone surrogate loss for CRC (Theorem 4). Credit and benchmark the prior methods, and rename baselines after their sources (Gaussian chance constraint after Blackmore 2011, worst-case after Bretl and Hutchinson 2013, CE-pair as Lindemann-style Bonferroni).
major_issues.effort: 2-3 days of literature work and writing.

major_issues.issue: Theory and experiment are inconsistent in several places, and the fixed-point implementation has a correctness gap. (a) The Theorem 1 upper bound 1-eps+1/(n+1) is stated for M=0, but fig5 shows 0.775 realised at target 0.70; the bound holds only for P(S<=q). (b) A4 (stationarity over k) and Theorem 2's 'subset of pairs' domination conflict with the terrain heterogeneity that motivates CE-A, because passes of different plans lie on different terrain. (c) Theorem 3 pools pair maxima within a run, which are not exchangeable; this is unresolved. (d) calibrate_conformal stops after iters=3 and returns q without checking q <= lam_ref. 14/60 paddy CE-U, 11/48 wheat CE-U and 22/48 wheat CE-A fields used 3 iterations, so convergence and domination are unverified there. (e) In the hard regime (w=1.5 m, RTK x3), naive calibration gives lambda = 0.52 against 0.28 for the full method at the same coverage of about 0.92. This is unexplained, and naive never under-covers, so Theorem 2 has no demonstrated failure case.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Theory reviewers will catch the overstated tightness and the contradictory assumptions. A silent non-convergence path undermines the certificate the paper is built on.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Restate Theorem 1 with the upper bound on S and explain the M-versus-S gap (empirically about 4.5% conservative; plot both in fig5). Replace A4 with conditional exchangeability given features, or prove domination under a monotone-coupling assumption. For Theorem 3, use one pair per run or cite the Barber et al. 2023 coverage-gap bound with a measured total-variation term. In code, raise or flag when the loop exits with q > lam_ref, raise iters to 10, and log the history. Build a regime where naive calibration fails: narrow implement plus heavy-tailed RTK so that N(q)/N(0) >= 1.5. Otherwise demote Theorem 2 to a remark.
major_issues.effort: Code fix and logging: 1 hour. Reruns: 1 day. Proof revisions: about 1 week of the authors' time.

major_issues.issue: System-level evaluation is missing. Only main-area overlap is measured. Headlands are excluded, fields are convex hulls of DBSCAN clusters, and there is no route, turn, path-length, time, fuel or input accounting, so the effect cannot be translated into farm value.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: T-ASE and agricultural reviewers expect system-level metrics. Convex-hull 'real fields' weaken the claim of real geometry, and a 1.8-percentage-point overlap difference is meaningless without cost translation.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Run the full Fields2Cover pipeline (headland generation, swath angle, route ordering, Dubins or continuous-curvature turns) with CE as the cov_width setter (w - 2q). Use concave hulls or alpha shapes plus boustrophedon decomposition for non-convex fields. Report total path length, number of turns, operating time, fuel, CNY/ha of inputs and missed m2/ha, with per-field paired differences against each competitor at equal reliability.

major_issues.issue: Statistics and reporting. Clopper-Pearson intervals pool about 8,000 runs across fields, which ignores field-level clustering and calibration-draw variability. The wheat cross-field comparison (E3b) has 1-2 repeats, with CI = nan for 5 of 8 methods. Holm p-values all equal the minimum achievable value, and effect sizes are not reported. The report (v2, 11 methods), tables (27/16 fields), figures (19/10) and CSVs (60/37, wheat still running) disagree.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Overstated precision and an unfinished, inconsistent evidence base are a common desk-reject reason at Q1.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Use a hierarchical bootstrap over fields and calibration draws. Report the per-field realised-coverage distribution against the theoretical Beta(n+1-l, l) envelope. Report effect sizes in passes, metres, minutes and CNY/ha with field-cluster CIs. Run at least 10 repeats for E3b on both crops. Freeze one experiment version and regenerate the report, tables and figures from it.
major_issues.effort: 1-2 days, plus 1-2 days of CPU for repeats.

major_issues.issue: Shift and out-of-distribution robustness is weak and not benchmarked. CE-U fails 3/10 real leave-one-block/day-out splits while scenario and PAC hold. Weighted CP shows no gain under the regional shifts tried. The only shift competitor is the method's own weighted version.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: Reviewers will conclude that the conservative PAC/scenario rule is preferable in deployment, which reverses the headline.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Benchmark against robust CP (Cauchois et al. 2024, f-divergence ball), PAC-CP, weighted CP with estimated density ratios (logistic-regression classifier on terrain and condition features), and Mondrian CP by block or day. Give a practitioner decision rule: marginal CE when exchangeable, PAC or robust CE when shift is suspected, ACI online. Use a shift that actually breaks exchangeability (calibrate on dry or flat fields, test on wet or hilly ones) so that weighting can matter.

major_issues.issue: Online adaptation (ACI) is compared only with static calibration. The real stream has 49 strips (K=3) or 24 (K=5), too short to show long-run frequency, and its curve is flat at zero for 38 strips.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: ACI is a 2021 method, and newer online-CP methods exist and are standard baselines.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Add DtACI (Gibbs and Candes 2024 JMLR), AgACI (Zaffran et al. 2022), conformal PID (Angelopoulos et al. 2023), SAOCP (Bhatnagar et al. 2023) and sliding-window recalibration on the soil-moisture drift simulation. Report long-run miss frequency, local coverage and cumulative overlap cost. Use the real stream only as a sanity check.
major_issues.effort: 1 day; each method is about 20 lines of code.

major_issues.issue: The generality claim (mowing, cleaning, UAV survey or spraying swaths) is unsupported, and the experiments report is outdated (describes v2 with 40 fields and 11 methods).
major_issues.concrete_fix: Either remove the claim or add one UAV swath case with real flight logs (PX4 ulog datasets on GitHub or S3, unverified). Rewrite the report from the frozen v3+ results.
major_issues.effort: 1 day to remove and rewrite; 3-4 days to add a UAV case if logs are found.

major_issues.issue: Venue targeting. Without real autonomous hardware runs, T-RO and RA-L are not realistic. T-ASE or CEA are realistic only after the P0 items are fixed.
major_issues.why_reviewer_would_reject: RA-L/T-RO reviewers routinely reject planning papers whose execution is fully simulated and whose real data is a replay of manual driving.
major_issues.concrete_fix: Primary target: IEEE T-ASE, with a strong 'Note to Practitioners' framing it as a certified overlap setting for any autosteer planner and controller. Alternative: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture or Biosystems Engineering, emphasising the economic analysis. Verify the CAS (中科院) and JCR partition of each journal before submitting.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Fields2Cover full CPP pipeline (headland, brute-force swath angle, boustrophedon/snake route, Dubins/CC turns)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: pip install fields2cover (v2.1.0 confirmed on PyPI). Feed the real field polygons; native overlap = fixed cov_width. Run F2C-native and F2C+CE (cov_width = w - 2q), then execute the swaths in the simulator. Report total path length, turns and time at equal reliability.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mier, Valente, de Bruin, 'Fields2Cover: An open-source coverage path planning library for unmanned agricultural vehicles', IEEE RA-L 8(4), 2023

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Side-to-side 3D coverage path planning that minimises skip/overlap between swaths
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Re-implement swath offsets computed on the DEM surface so that projected 3D footprints abut. Deterministic terrain compensation with no statistics; compare it natively and with CE on top. This is the closest prior art for the skip/overlap objective.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Hameed, la Cour-Harbo, Osen, Robotics and Autonomous Systems 76:36-45, 2016

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Coverage path planning on 3D terrain for arable farming
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Re-implement the slope-dependent effective-width model and the terrain-aware choice of driving direction; use it as the planner layer and compare it natively and with CE.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Jin and Tang, Journal of Field Robotics 28(3):424-440, 2011

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Robust coverage under bounded position error (footprint erosion by a worst-case bound)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Erode by a model-based error bound (tube radius or spec +/-2.5 cm at 3 sigma) rather than the max calibration score; credit the current 'Robust worst-case' baseline to this work.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Bretl and Hutchinson, 'Robust coverage by a mobile robot of a planar workspace', ICRA 2013

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Boustrophedon cellular decomposition / GTSP boustrophedon for non-convex fields
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Needed to drop the convex-hull approximation. Implement BCD in shapely or port the ETH ASL polygon_coverage_planning logic (GitHub) and plug CE into each cell.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Choset, Autonomous Robots 9, 2000; Bahnemann et al., 'Revisiting boustrophedon coverage path planning as a generalized traveling salesman problem', FSR 2019

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Slip-compensated adaptive path tracking for farm vehicles
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Add a sideslip observer and adaptive control law to core.simulate as a new ctrl option. Run it with fixed overlap and with CE, to test whether better control alone makes the certificate unnecessary.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Lenain, Thuilot, Cariou, Martinet, Autonomous Robots 21:79-97, 2006

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Robust tube MPC with constraint tightening (and deterministic tube erosion of the swath)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Linear lateral-error model (d, psi, integral) with the disturbance set from calibration residuals; RPI set via pytope; MPC via cvxpy/OSQP or casadi (all on PyPI). Baseline: erode by the tube radius. Ours: CE plus tube MPC with a tightened B in CE-R.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Mayne, Seron, Rakovic, Automatica 41(2), 2005; agricultural variant: Kayacan et al., IEEE/ASME T-Mech 20(1), 2015

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Cautious GP-MPC / GP-based uncertainty margin
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Fit a sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor from slope and condition features to pass-to-pass error; margin = z_{1-eps} * sigma_GP (uncalibrated Bayesian). The proposal lists this baseline but never implemented it.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Gaussian chance-constrained planning with iterative risk allocation
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Per-pair Gaussian models; allocate eps_k non-uniformly across pass pairs to minimise passes (IRA). This is the principled competitor to CE-pair's uniform Bonferroni split; credit the 'Gaussian chance constr.' baseline to Blackmore.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Ono and Williams, CDC 2008; Blackmore, Ono, Williams, IEEE T-RO 27(6), 2011

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal prediction for safe planning with a union bound over time
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: This is exactly CE-pair; rename it and credit it as Lindemann-style per-step CP with a Bonferroni split.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Lindemann, Cleaveland, Shim, Pappas, IEEE RA-L 8(8), 2023

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: CP regions for time series with optimised normalisation weights (LCP)
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: On a held-out split, optimise per-terrain-bin sigma weights to minimise total eroded width subject to coverage (scipy milp or linprog). This is both a competitor and the principled fix for the CE-A null result.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: PAC / training-conditional conformal prediction
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Choose the order statistic r with BetaCDF(1-eps; r, n+1-r) <= delta. With n=100 and delta=0.05 this gives r=96, the same as the scenario approach. It is the fair counterpart for scenario; report both guarantee types.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Vovk, ACML 2012; Park, Bastani, Matni, Lee, ICLR 2020

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Sample average approximation of chance constraints
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Empirical (1-eps) quantile of the run score with no finite-sample correction; one line. Shows how much the conformal finite-sample correction costs.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Luedtke and Ahmed, SIAM J. Optim. 19(2), 2008

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal prediction with conditional guarantees
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Quantile regression over a function class of terrain features (side slope, direction, edge distance) with conditional coverage; competitor for CE-A.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Distributionally robust conformal prediction
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Inflate the quantile level for an f-divergence ball of radius rho; benchmark on leave-one-block/day-out and plain-to-hilly shifts against weighted CP and PAC.

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Online CP: DtACI, AgACI, conformal PID, SAOCP
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Drop-in replacements for the ACI update in the drift experiment and the real stream; report long-run and local coverage plus overlap cost.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Gibbs and Candes JMLR 2024; Zaffran et al. ICML 2022; Angelopoulos, Candes, Tibshirani NeurIPS 2023; Bhatnagar et al. ICML 2023

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Adaptive CP for motion planning / conformal decision theory
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Use as online and decision-level competitors in the related-work positioning; implement the conformal decision theory risk-control update on lambda as an alternative to ACI.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Dixit et al., L4DC 2023; Lekeufack et al., ICRA 2024

competitor_algorithms_requested.name: Conformal Predictive Programming
competitor_algorithms_requested.how_to_implement_here: Shows that with a 1-D decision CPP reduces to the conformal-erosion quantile. Discuss it and run it with the 2-D decision (lambda, driving angle) once certified angle optimisation is added.
competitor_algorithms_requested.reference: Zhao et al., arXiv 2402.07407, 2024 (journal version unverified)
